intro.note: Answer each question in your workbook. Show your working.
methodSteps: 1  Identify the value of each digit
2  Compare from the largest place value
commonMistakes: Confusing the value of a digit with the digit itself (the 3 in 35,000 is worth 30,000).
When comparing numbers with different lengths, the longer number is larger.
Always line up digits by place value — start from the left.
workedExample: Step 1 — Identify place values: all have 4 thousands.
Step 2 — Compare hundreds: 4,052 has 0; the others have 5.
Step 3 — Compare tens of remaining two: 4,502 < 4,520.
intro.visualAid: Place value chart showing columns: Millions | Hundred-Thousands | Ten-Thousands | Thousands | Hundreds | Tens | Ones — with the number 5,040,683 broken into its digit columns.

questions.content: Write down the value of the 6 in: a) 6,421  b) 3,602  c) 46,000  d) 609,000
A 5-digit number: ten-thousands = 7, hundreds = 4, rest = 0. Write the number.
Cards: 3  0  7  5  2. Using each once, make a) the largest 5-digit number  b) the smallest 5-digit number.
Midnight temp = −4 °C. By noon it rose 11°. What is the temperature at noon?
Populations: Ashford 125,400; Bexley 125,040; Croydon 152,400. a) Order smallest first. b) Ashford +3,000 — now larger than Croydon? Explain.
6-digit number clues: hundred-thousands = tens + 1; tens = 4; between 500,000–600,000; ones = half hundreds; hundreds = 8; thousands & ten-thousands = 0. Find it.
